title: TITAN: A Fast and Distributed Large-Scale Trapped-Ion NISQ Computer
problem: Distributed trapped-ion quantum computers suffer from significant entanglement latency across photonic switches and generate suboptimal qubit mappings because existing compilers lack awareness of the interconnection topology.
motivation: Trapped-ion technology offers extended coherence times and high gate fidelity, making it promising for large-scale NISQ systems if system-level communication and compilation challenges can be addressed.
method: TITAN introduces an innovative photonic interconnection design reducing entanglement latency across distributed Quantum Charge Coupled Devices (QCCDs). It employs a topology-aware partitioning and mapping algorithm that optimizes matter-link communications and qubit placement, connecting multiple QCCDs via quantum matter-links and photonic switches.
key_novelty: A topology-aware compiler algorithm combined with optimized photonic interconnection design to minimize entanglement latency in distributed trapped-ion NISQ systems.
contributions: Innovative photonic interconnection design reducing entanglement latency
Topology-aware partitioning and mapping algorithm optimizing matter-link communications
56.6% performance improvement and 19.7% fidelity improvement over existing systems
primary_theme: Distributed quantum computing with optimized photonic interconnects
